drivingQuestion: What is Rabbi Eliezer's source for holding that a threshold year counts as below until a month and a day have passed?
outcomeNote: The baraita supplies Rabbi Eliezer's verbal analogy; nothing is raised against it in this unit.

segments.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ יְתֵירוֹת עַל הַשָּׁנִים חוֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד. תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״לְמַעְלָה״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״חֹדֶשׁ וָמַעְלָה״, מָה לְהַלָּן מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד, אַף כָּאן מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Eliezer says:» Their halakhic status remains like that of the period preceding it, «until they will be» aged one «month and one day beyond the» respective «years.» With regard to this opinion, it «is taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Eliezer says: It is stated here,» with regard to valuations, «“upward”» (Leviticus 27:7), «and it is stated there,» with regard to the census of the Levites in the wilderness: “From «one month old and upward» you shall number them” (Numbers 3:15). «Just as there,» in the case of the census, the verse means: «From one month and one day old, so too here,» with regard to valuations, the verse means that each respective category is counted «from» one «month and one day old» beyond the stated ages of five years, twenty years, or sixty years.
